notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf107:l001: The final word is provisionally жабуусун; the compressed middle strokes could conceal a different possessive ending. The object continues the preceding page.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf107:l002: The initial consonant of Паана and the final ң of бараның are not fully distinct; retain this reading rather than regularizing to баана.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf107:l004: Алда is the apparent written form of the divine name; not silently expanded to Алла. The connected лд strokes remain uncertain.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf107:l005: The ending of карааның may instead be караанын; the second-person possessive and hence the English pronoun are provisional.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf107:l006: The last word is difficult: provisionally кырааның, an epithet for champions; кыраалын is another possible letter sequence. The English renders the provisional epithet.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf107:l017: The final word appears авам, including manuscript в; авасы is possible from the ending. The first-person shift is retained provisionally. A pencil underline and small cross do not erase the verse.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf107:l019: The adjective before кылыч is provisionally Кыяндуу; its joined middle letters are difficult, possibly Кыяптуу. Formidable is a tentative contextual rendering.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf107:l021: The first word looks Заар; каар would be idiomatic but is not substituted for the visible initial. The English takes заар as fierceness or venom.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf107:l031: The adjective looks оңкон, but that positive meaning conflicts with the following ominous lines. A negative form may have been intended; no invisible negative syllable is supplied. English follows the provisional visible reading.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf107:l034: The final word appears авам, matching l017, but the possessive ending and the resulting change of voice are uncertain. Manuscript в is retained rather than modernized to б.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf107:l035: The word дүйнөгө has compressed medial strokes; the reading and its interpretation as the afterlife are provisional. The subject is left implicit as in the manuscript.
